title: Bounded-occurrence Max-E3LIN2

problem.name: Bounded-occurrence Max-E3LIN2
problem.statement_latex:
Given $m$ equations $x_a\oplus x_b\oplus x_c=b_j$ over $\mathbb F_2$, with every variable appearing in at most $D$ equations, maximize the number satisfied. Random assignment satisfies half in expectation; the approximation question measures the additive improvement over $1/2$.
Complexity counts quantum gates for QAOA, classical arithmetic time for approximation, and bit operations for exact bounded-degree instances.

quantum.headline_latex: $O(m+n)$ gates per sample, $p=1$ QAOA for bounded-occurrence Max-E3LIN2.
quantum.details_latex: For sufficiently large $D$, the guaranteed satisfied fraction is at least $1/2+1/(101\sqrt D\ln D)$. The theorem chooses parameters from the objective analysis; shot counts for estimating the objective and success amplification contribute additional costs.

quantum.details_text: For sufficiently large $D$, the guaranteed satisfied fraction is at least $1/2+1/(101\sqrt D\ln D)$. The theorem chooses parameters from the objective analysis; shot counts for estimating the objective and success amplification contribute additional costs.

classical.headline_latex: Polynomial time with fraction $1/2+\Omega(D^{-1/2})$, Barak et al.; $\operatorname{poly}(n)2^{O_D(n/\sqrt{\log n})}$ for exact optimization at fixed $D$.
classical.details_latex: The classical approximation algorithm applies to odd-arity XOR constraints and improves the dependence on $D$ in the QAOA guarantee. At fixed occurrence bound, $m=O(n)$ and the exact objective threshold has a linear-size Boolean circuit. Exact counting, binary search and witness recovery supply the displayed bit-complexity bound.

strength.description_latex: The approximation guarantee has a polynomial-time classical comparator with a stronger dependence on $D$. The stated quantum algorithm has no established runtime advantage.

hardware.description_latex: A QAOA circuit uses $n$ data qubits and coherent three-body parity phases, typically decomposed into two-qubit gates. Modest instances are feasible on circuit hardware; scaling depends on connectivity, noise and sampling cost.
